memories.memory_text: I saw Eric stumble and fall over as I was gaining on him during the chase along the beach.

memories.memory_text: I was standing near the saddling enclosure in my chauffeur's uniform, trying to blend in with the well-dressed men around me.

grounded_facts: Carter removes Eric's sunglasses and mocks his eye color, belittling his attempt at respectability.
memories.memory_text: I remember Carter taking my sunglasses off my face and staring into my eyes before saying they still looked like piss holes in the snow.

grounded_facts: Through sarcasm and personal remarks, Carter demonstrates familiarity with Eric’s history and criminal background, undermining Eric's attempt to appear reformed.
memories.memory_text: I got the sense Carter was mocking me on purpose, hinting he knew about my past and didn't believe my act of being reformed, though he never said it outright.

grounded_facts: Carter identifies and approaches Eric Paice, who is disguised in a chauffeur's uniform, initiating a tense and probing conversation.
Carter persistently asks Eric who he is working for, rejecting his claim of being 'straight'.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carter spot me at the racetrack and walk over. He started questioning me, asking who I was working for, pushing when I said I was straight, and even took off my sunglasses to stare me down.

grounded_facts: Carter asks Eric if he knows a man named Albert Swift, marking a shift in focus toward gathering intelligence.
Carter asks Eric if he knows a man named Albert Swift, seeking potential intelligence.
memories.memory_text: I remember Carter asking me if I knew a man named Albert Swift, shifting the conversation like he was testing me, trying to get information out of me.

grounded_facts: Kinnear dismisses Ray from the room, reinforcing the social hierarchy.
memories.memory_text: I heard Kinnear tell Ray to 'piss off' right after Carter passed by, and I saw Ray leave—it was clear Kinnear was reasserting control over the room.

grounded_facts: A high-stakes poker game attended by Kinnear, Harry, Peter, Les, and Eric, with Carter arriving mid-game.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting on the sofa with Glenda during the poker game, watching Kinnear, Harry, Peter, and Les play, feeling the tension of the high stakes in the room.

grounded_facts: Carter enters the sitting room, interrupting the poker game, and is acknowledged by Kinnear and the others.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carter walk in and blow a kiss to Ray, then glance back at the table where Kinnear pushed in more money—I noticed how everyone acknowledged his presence even as he seemed bored.

grounded_facts: Glenda repeatedly draws Carter's attention, revealing a prior connection to Sid Fletcher and positioning herself physically to attract him.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Glenda kept drawing Carter's attention, tucking her legs up to catch his eye, and later I heard her say they had gone about together, hinting at a past with Sid Fletcher.

grounded_facts: Kinnear reveals a hearts flush, queen high, after Harry calls his bluff, winning the hand.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kinnear reveal a flush—queen high in hearts—after Harry called his bluff, and he won the hand right then.

grounded_facts: Kinnear mocks Harry for doubting his bluff, undermining Harry's confidence in front of others.
memories.memory_text: I heard Kinnear mock Harry for doubting his bluff, and it was clear he was undermining him in front of all of us.

grounded_facts: Carter implies Harry will quickly lose his money, reinforcing the high-stakes tension of the game.
memories.memory_text: I heard Carter say Harry would lose his money quickly, and after the hand ended, he reminded Harry it hadn't taken long, which kept the tension high.

grounded_facts: Carter leaves the sitting room after the poker hand concludes, signaling his disengagement from the gathering.
memories.memory_text: I opened the door and followed Carter out of the sitting room after the hand ended, signaling I was done with the gathering too.

grounded_facts: Eric expresses disapproval of Carter's actions and reveals that Cyril, Sid, and Gerald may retaliate if they learn of Carter's interference.
memories.memory_text: I told Carter I didn't like what he did, and that Cyril wouldn't like it either—especially since he didn't know who Carter was really working for. I made it clear that Sid and Gerald wouldn't take it well if they found out he'd been interfering.

grounded_facts: Carter exits after a confrontational exchange with Eric, indicating a breakdown in trust and escalating tension.
memories.memory_text: After our talk, I saw Carter leave, and I knew things between us had changed—there was no trust left.

grounded_facts: After Carter departs, Eric silently instructs Ray to pursue or monitor Carter's movements.
memories.memory_text: Once Carter was gone, I signaled to Ray to follow him so we could keep track of where he went.

grounded_facts: The Girl in the cafe calls Eric to inform him that Carter has come for Albert, speculating he arrived on the ferry.
memories.memory_text: I was told by the girl in the cafe that Carter had come for Albert, and she thought he arrived on the ferry.

grounded_facts: Carter is informed that he has been betrayed by Anna, which changes his understanding of the situation and his relationship with her.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Con that he had informed Gerald about Carter and Anna, which confirmed the betrayal and gave me the leverage to break Carter emotionally.

grounded_facts: Carter shoots and kills Peter after gaining the upper hand on the ferry roof.
Carter commands Peter to stay still and then shoots him dead, establishing lethal control.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carter gain the upper hand on Peter and shoot him dead, even after telling him to stay still — it felt like a cold, controlled act of dominance.

grounded_facts: Eric taunts Carter about Anna being with Gerald, aiming to emotionally wound him.
memories.memory_text: I taunted Carter, telling him Gerald was probably with Anna right now and asking if he'd still fancy her when Gerald finished with her face, aiming to crush him.

grounded_facts: Eric signals for Carter's car to be pushed into the river and destroyed.
Eric has Carter's car pushed into the river while delivering a mocking remark.
memories.memory_text: I mocked Carter by telling him his car needed a wash, then I signaled for it to be pushed into the river and destroyed.

grounded_facts: A tense standoff occurs as the ferry arrives, involving verbal taunts, gunfire, betrayal revelations, a killing, and vehicle destruction.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the whole standoff when the ferry arrived—Carter was isolated, we moved into position, Con and I mocked him, and I gave the signal to push his car into the water to assert control.

grounded_facts: A large party at The Heights with loud music, attended by rich-looking middle-aged men and young women, featuring dancing in one room and blue movies in another.
memories.memory_text: I remember the party at The Heights was loud and crowded, with rich-looking older men and young women everywhere, dancing in one room and blue movies playing in another.

memories.memory_text: I was on the phone and then went over to Kinnear to tell him that Gerald Fletcher wanted a word with him.

grounded_facts: A private exchange initiated by Cyril with Eric in the library during a party.
memories.memory_text: I remember Cyril pulling me aside in the library during the party, initiating a private exchange between us.

grounded_facts: Cyril explicitly asks to speak with Eric, indicating intent for a private or significant exchange.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Cyril say, 'Yes, Eric. A word with you,' clearly indicating he wanted a private or significant conversation.

grounded_facts: A social gathering still ongoing inside the house at dawn.
memories.memory_text: I could tell the party was still going inside, even though I was stepping out into the dawn.

grounded_facts: Eric exits the house where the party is ongoing and departs in a Cadillac.
memories.memory_text: I came out the front door and got into my Cadillac, then drove away from the house.

grounded_facts: Carter mocks Paice's running ability while chasing him overhead on the jetty.
memories.memory_text: I heard Carter mock me from above on the jetty, saying I couldn't win an egg and spoon race.

grounded_facts: Paice, wheezing, tells Carter to go away in response to the taunt.
memories.memory_text: I was wheezing as I shouted back at him, telling him to sod off.

grounded_facts: Carter arrives at the coal jetty with a shotgun and Scotch, spots Eric Paice, and initiates pursuit after Paice flees upon seeing him.
memories.memory_text: I was at the coal jetty at dawn when I saw Carter arrive with a shotgun and a bottle of Scotch; the moment he spotted me, I knew I had to run.

grounded_facts: Carter aims his shotgun at Paice and threatens to shoot if Paice approaches the parked car.
Carter points his shotgun at Paice and threatens to kill him if he approaches the car.
memories.memory_text: I saw Carter raise his shotgun and point it at me, and he shouted, 'Stay away from the car or I'll blow you apart,' so I froze and knew he'd shoot if I moved toward it.

grounded_facts: A pursuit unfolds between Carter and Eric Paice across multiple levels of a coal jetty at dawn, involving evasion, verbal taunting, and armed threat.
memories.memory_text: I kept sprinting across the jetty, dodging down stairways and under structures, always hearing Carter above me taunting me like a game, knowing he had the shotgun and was chasing me.

grounded_facts: Eric arrives on the beach, running with visible distress.
memories.memory_text: I ran onto the beach, my breath ragged and painful, feet pounding over the pebbles as I pushed forward in distress.

grounded_facts: Carter appears and watches Eric from a distance before descending to the beach.
memories.memory_text: I was running on the beach and stumbling along, and I realized Carter had appeared and was watching me from a distance before starting to come down.

grounded_facts: Eric stumbles and falls over as Carter gains on him during a chase along the beach.
memories.memory_text: I stumbled and fell while running from Carter along the beach, panic surging through me as he gained on me.

grounded_facts: After falling and getting up, Eric flees and disappears from view around the headland, evading immediate capture.
memories.memory_text: I got back on my feet quickly and kept fleeing, vanishing around the headland to escape Carter's reach.

grounded_facts: Eric is found in a difficult physical situation, half-way along a desolate beach, struggling in the mud.
memories.memory_text: I was stuck in the mud, struggling to move as I lay half-way along that desolate beach.

memories.memory_text: I saw Carter closing in on me, moving steadily across the beach as the confrontation between us began to unfold.

grounded_facts: Eric stumbles and falls near the top of the narrow valley, too exhausted to get up initially.
memories.memory_text: I stumbled and fell near the top of the narrow valley, and I was so exhausted I couldn't get up at first.

grounded_facts: Carter verbally accuses Eric of causing his brother Frank's death by forcing him to drink whisky.
Carter verbally connects Eric's forced drinking to the incident where Eric poured whisky down Frank (Carter's brother) before his death.
memories.memory_text: I remember Carter forcing me to drink whisky while yelling at me, saying I poured it down his brother Frank’s throat and that I caused his death, just like this.

grounded_facts: Carter offers Eric a drink in a mocking tone, referencing dark past events.
memories.memory_text: I remember Carter mocking me, offering me a drink and taunting me about the past, saying things like 'Drink up, son. Just like it was with my brother, Frank.'

grounded_facts: Carter repeatedly orders Eric to continue drinking despite his choking and retching.
memories.memory_text: I kept choking and retching, but Carter just kept yelling 'Drink up!' and 'Don't stop, Eric!'—he wouldn't let me stop no matter how much I struggled.

grounded_facts: A violent encounter between Carter and Eric in the narrow valley where Eric is forced to drink whisky and is ultimately struck down.
memories.memory_text: I was on the ground when Carter caught up and demanded I stand, then forced me to drink whisky from a bottle, pouring it into my mouth even as it spilled down my face, and when I couldn't take it all, he raised the butt of his shotgun and struck me in the head.

grounded_facts: After forcing Eric to drink and choke, Carter strikes Eric on the head with the butt of his shotgun, killing him.
memories.memory_text: I was panting and scrambling up the valley, trying to get away, but Carter caught up and forced me to drink whisky from a bottle—he kept telling me to drink it all, just like with his brother Frank. I could barely keep it down, it spilled down my face, and he asked if we laughed when Frank was spewing. I looked at him, but there was no mercy in his eyes. Then he lifted the bottle again, held the shotgun, and finally raised the butt and brought it down on my head.

grounded_facts: Carter makes Eric drink an entire bottle of Scotch, pouring it into his mouth and insisting he continue despite choking.
memories.memory_text: I felt the whisky being poured into my mouth, and I couldn't stop it—Carter forced me to drink the whole bottle, holding the gun to my head while I choked and spilled it down my face.

grounded_facts: Eric's body is transported via a coal bucket along a cable and dropped into the sea, followed by coal slag, marking the end of his physical presence.
memories.memory_text: I remember my body being loaded into a coal bucket, moving off along a cable on its final journey, dropping into the sea, followed by coal slag and black dust, and then the waves closing over — everything gone.

memories.memory_text: I reached through the letterbox, felt the cold metal of the key, and pulled it out to open the door—my own house, but it didn’t feel like coming home.

I moved around Frank’s coffin with the razor in hand, the cord stretched tight from the lamp above him—my reflection flickered in the blade as I shaved, the hum of the motor the only sound in the room.
I was watching Frank’s coffin ahead when Keith said he couldn’t believe it—he was surprised Frank didn’t show up for work. Said he was always on time.
Eddie muttered it was a bloody funny thing—Frank was calm, like gentle Jesus, for six years, then suddenly did something like this. I just said, yeah, a bloody funny thing.
I asked Keith, 'Since when did he drink whisky?' and saw the doubt flicker across his face—nobody had an answer, nobody even knew.
I leaned in and told Keith to let me know if anyone asked for me—set myself up as someone looking, someone watching. Then I asked about Albert Swift, knowing he might be the first real lead.
I walked past Ray and blew him a kiss just as he was trying to sound tough—I could see the surprise on his face, and Kinnear didn’t stop me, so I knew I’d already taken the room.
When Kinnear offered condolences about Frank, I just said 'Yep'—short, no emotion, because showing anything would’ve been weakness, and he needed to see I wasn’t here to grieve, I was here to push.

I stood by that crushed Hillman in the scrapyard and asked Billy Laws if the steering was faulty—then the brakes. He said both were fine. When he told me Frank was drunk, I just said, 'Was he?' like I didn’t believe it, or didn’t want to.

I picked up the wooden casket from the hall table, felt its weight—lighter than I expected—and put it on the side table without opening it. When Edna asked if Frank was staying the night, I just said, 'Funny.'
I looked at Edna and told her I fancied her, that I wanted to touch her, to make love to her—then asked her softly, 'Where are you?'
I asked Anna if she was wearing the sexy, silk ones, then told her to take her bra off—she hesitated, but I told her again, softly, to go on.
I told him to move slowly, to imagine it was me doing it—my voice, my presence, like I was there in his skin.
I took the ticket Thorpe handed me, smiled, and asked who to thank—knowing full well it wasn’t a favor, but a threat.
I tore the ticket in half and threw it in the gutter—then yanked the car door open and slammed it into the man getting out, shattering the window and spraying blood.

I pulled the chain in the stall while Thorpe was sitting there, watching the door like a cornered animal—he bolted upright, scared out of his wits before I even spoke. Then I told him, 'Time's up, Thorpey,' and smiled; he knew the game was over.
I picked up Frank's casket on the stairs.
I opened the door, pushed Thorpe inside, and shut Edna out. When she threatened the police, I told her no, you won't—and I knew she wouldn't.
I had Thorpe doubled over in pain, screaming—he finally spat out 'Brumby' after I squeezed hard. I knew he could talk if he wanted to.
After Thorpe gasped out 'Burnham,' I connected Brumby to the arcades along the coast—Keith even confirmed he'd been to Westsea. The pieces were falling into place.
I saw Brumby get out of his white Bentley and kick a young man into the lily pond after yelling about someone spewing on his goldfish.

I parked and watched from behind a tree. I saw Brumby arrive and storm into the house. He shouted at Sandra, then passed an upstairs window while she locked herself in a bedroom. I heard him yell, 'Unlock the door, you bitch.' I opened the front door and went in.
I said I made a mistake—twice—because Thorpe lied; Brumby didn't recognize me or the Fletchers, and that laugh came out before I could stop it, cold and sharp in the quiet room.
I was with Edna, the bedsprings moving gently, and then her laughter—just before the door opened and their legs appeared, blocking the light.
I covered Con with the shotgun, took his gun, and made him open the coalshed door before bolting him inside—then got in the car and left.

I didn't believe her when she said Frank threatened to kill himself after she turned him down. Frank wasn't like that—he was too careful, too controlled. I snapped her sunglasses in half just to shut out the lie, but it still rang in my head.

I grabbed her arm and shouted in her face—she had to know I wasn't leaving until I found out who killed Frank. Then I saw Peter's Jaguar coming, and when Con called my name, I knew she'd ratted me out. I hit her and jumped the rail before they could reach me.
I remember asking Glenda how she found me, and then her slamming the car to a stop, saying the demon king had sent her with a spell—some twisted certainty that I’d show up.
Brumby offered me five thousand dollars and the name Cyril Kinnear, saying he was responsible for Frank's death—but I didn't believe him. That wasn't enough to make me act.
I asked Glenda who set her up in the apartment, and she said Brumby—simple as that. Then she told me Kinnear doesn’t suspect a thing because he thinks she’s simple.

I turned on the projector after she left the room and saw the film—'The Teacher's Pet'—with Glenda bare-breasted in front of a blackboard, then Margaret offering a schoolgirl a ride in a car. I didn’t see the girl’s face, but it was clear what kind of operation this was.
I stood over Glenda in the bath and asked about the girl in the film, and when she kept lying, I grabbed her and held her under the water until she coughed up the name—Doreen.
When she said the girl was Doreen, I told her the name Carter wasn't just mine—it was hers too, her father was my brother Frank, and he was murdered, and I made her get out of the bath.
I raised the shotgun to throw it clear into the sea—just let it go—and then something hit me hard, like a punch from nowhere, and I fell.

memories.memory_text: I was named under pressure—Thorpe screamed my name when Carter twisted him, and suddenly I wasn't just a rumor anymore.
Carter knew about the arcades—how the machines along the coast, the ones people fed pennies into, were mine.
I kicked that puke-stained kid face-first into the lily pond—right where he was spewing all over my goldfish. This is my house, my rules, and I'll not have some tosser trashing it.
I banged on Sandra's door, shouting for her to unlock it—she thinks she can shut me out, but this is still my house and she's not locking me out like some stranger.

I confronted that bastard in my sitting room, demanding to know who sent him at two in the morning, and when he just stood there laughing, I swung at him—next thing I knew, my head was ringing and I was collapsing into the chair, hurt and humiliated.
I wasn't even there when they brought up my name—just some joke between Carter and Edna, like I’m something to laugh about.

I offered Carter five grand and the name Cyril Kinnear, trying to make it clear we had the same enemy, but he walked out, shouting it wasn't good enough—like I was just another liar trying to use him.
I set her up in that apartment, and I made sure there was a projector—she knows what it’s for, especially when she’s the one on screen.
I saw the film and I wanted to meet Doreen — that’s what I told Albert when I paid him a visit.
I told them I didn't want any cooking in the restaurant—just put a hatch in the wall. Then that bloody car screeched up, and I had to go see who the madman was.
I came out to the top tier.

I was coming down the stairs when Carter suddenly appeared and punched me hard in the gut—knocked the wind out of me. I barely got out that I had to show the film to Frank, that it was the only way to get at them.
I lined up the shot through the scope, saw Carter by the water, raised the rifle, and pulled the trigger—just a quiet whoosh, then he went down.

memories.memory_text: I swung around when Carter said my name—didn't see him coming, heart just dropped. Grey suit, cap, glasses—I thought I was hidden.
He took my sunglasses off, looked right into my eyes—called them piss holes in the snow. Felt exposed, like he saw through everything.
I'm gripping the wheel, tired as hell but pushing through—champagne corks popping behind me, voices buzzing, the radio spitting out race results while I keep the Cadillac steady down the road.
I jumped up when Ray said Carter was here—then Kinnear dropped it, said I worked for him, like it was some kind of joke. Carter looked at me like he saw through everything.
I told Carter straight—Cyril didn't like what he was doing, and Sid and Gerald wouldn't like it either. Then I made Ray follow after him.
They named me. Carter asked if I set it up, and Glenda said yeah. Now he thinks I pulled her.
I hear the girl's voice on the phone—'Eric, he's come for Albert'—and I know it's about me, even though I don't see her. The call tightens my chest, makes me move faster.
I brought Doreen in, used my connection through Margaret. Didn't think it'd go this far.
I stepped off the Land Rover, legs unsteady on the gangplank—the jetty swayed underfoot, water slapping below. The ferry was already chugging in, engine loud, no time to stop.

I laughed and told Carter he was finished. I said I'd bloody finished him. I told Con to tell Carter I'd told Gerald about him and Anna. I asked if Gerald believed us at first, then said Peter talked to him.
I laughed and told Carter his car needed a wash — then gave the signal. The Land Rover hit the Sunbeam twice, and it went into the river.
I told Kinnear Gerald wanted to speak to him—had to shout over the music just to be heard. Phone was hot in my hand, whole place buzzing like a damn hive.
Kinnear looked at me while talking to Carter, said something about it being arranged—like I’m part of some deal now. I kept pouring my drink, hands shaky, didn’t trust that look.
Kinnear called me out—just my name, calm like it was nothing, but it wasn't nothing. I was moving, always moving, but his voice made me stop.
I stepped out into the cold dawn air, the noise of the party still pounding behind me, and got into the Cadillac fast—just drove.
I bolted down the stairs and sprinted for the road, lungs burning, knowing he was up there somewhere—always above me, footsteps echoing just out of reach.
I saw the car—maybe a way out—then froze when I saw the gun raised above me; his voice cut through the dawn, and I ducked under the jetty instead.
I'm running across the beach, pebbles crunching under my feet, lungs burning with every breath. I can see the factory smoke in the distance, and then—Carter’s there, watching me.
I tripped and went down hard on the beach—sand in my mouth, heart slamming—Carter right behind me. Got up fast, didn’t look back, just ran around the headland.
I'm sinking in the black mud, each step dragging like my legs are made of lead, and I can see Carter gaining on me out of the corner of my eye.

I took the cap off the bottle, hands shaking, and poured the whisky into my mouth—couldn't stop it from spilling, burning down my face, suit soaked, Carter yelling in my ear about Frank, about the laugh, about the car.
I was choking, couldn't breathe, legs gave way—then the gun came down, hard, blacked out fast, didn't even see it coming.
I'm falling—cold, weightless—then the water hits hard, black dust choking the light as the waves close over me.
